name: delivery
description: portitor's release pipeline: how the `portitor` binary gets from a tagged commit to a downloadable, verifiable artifact. Binaries only — the gate image is built locally by `portitor deploy` with Nix, never published; this module also owns that deploy step. Generic module: the executable `.goreleaser.yaml` and the CI workflow files are the source of truth for how artifacts are built; this module documents intent and does not define a bespoke delivery-metadata schema. NOTE: this module.json is a hand-authored SEED in spexmachina's format — identity hashes (requirement id/preq_id, component spec_node_id) and spec/.snapshot.json are generated when run through `spex` / the /spec skill; they are intentionally omitted here.

requirements.title: Cross-architecture binary release
requirements.description: Release builds target linux and darwin, each amd64 and arm64 (four targets, no windows — portitor is a git-server-side gate, never installed on an agent's machine). `.goreleaser.yaml`'s build matrix (goos × goarch) is the sole definition of the target set.

requirements.title: Tiered CI by trigger
requirements.description: pull_request runs the fast gate (go build, go vet, go test). push to main runs the same gate plus `-race`. A nightly schedule fuzzes every `func Fuzz*` discovered in the tree (spec/reviews/2026-07-18.md §5's plan), each under a bounded -fuzztime, with no hardcoded target list to fall out of sync as targets are added. pull_request and push to main also run the docker tier (a real daemon with userns-remap, `go test -tags docker`, no secrets) and the acceptance tier (`go test -tags acceptance` against a disposable GitHub repo, its PAT limited to Contents, Pull requests and Actions on that one private repo with no Workflows permission, reaching the test step's env only; the repo's seed, its one workflow included, is prepared by the operator and the suite only verifies and resets to it — see arch_ci.md); both install Nix with a commit-pinned action and a pinned Nix version and cache the store. The acceptance tier assumes people push portitor's branches; once agents do, a policy freezing `.github/**` for them must come first. push of a `v*` tag runs the release pipeline. Each workflow except the acceptance one sets `concurrency: {cancel-in-progress: true}` scoped to its own ref; the acceptance workflow uses one global, non-cancelling group, because every run resets the same disposable repo, and the CI workflow ignores docs-only changes (`**.md`, `spec/**`) so prose edits don't burn a runner.

requirements.title: Signed release artifacts
requirements.description: Every release archive is signed with SSHSIG (`ssh-keygen -Y sign -n file`, Ed25519) via GoReleaser's `signs` block, producing one `.sig` per archive. The secret key is supplied to the release workflow as the `SSH_SIGNING_KEY` repository secret, written to a runner-local temp file (chmod 600) for the duration of the job and removed afterward — the key material never appears in an argv or a template-expanded command line. The corresponding public key is published in README.md so a downloader can verify with `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against an `allowed_signers` line offline, independent of GitHub's availability.

requirements.title: SLSA build provenance
requirements.description: `actions/attest-build-provenance` runs in the release workflow (permissions `id-token: write`, `attestations: write`) over every published archive, producing an attestation verifiable with `gh attestation verify` — a second, GitHub-native chain of custody independent of the SSHSIG signature.

requirements.title: Machine-readable release manifest
requirements.description: `scripts/generate-manifest.sh` derives `manifest.json` from GoReleaser's own `dist/artifacts.json` (per-archive name/goos/goarch/format) and `dist/metadata.json` (version/commit/date) — recomputing each artifact's sha256 and size directly from the archive bytes on disk rather than trusting an internal field name, so the manifest is self-verifying against what actually shipped. Shape: `{schema_version, tool, version, git_sha, git_ref, built_at, status, artifacts:[{name, target, sha256, size_bytes, archive_format}]}`. It is attached to the GitHub release alongside the binaries so a downstream consumer (e.g. a Nix overlay) can pin a per-target checksum programmatically instead of hand-copying it out of a release page. The shape is generic — no portitor-specific field — and it is a derived, disposable projection: `.goreleaser.yaml` remains the one source of truth for how artifacts are actually built.

requirements.title: Binaries-only release channel
requirements.description: The GitHub Releases page is the only publication channel: each release carries the four archives, a consolidated `checksums.txt`, one `.sha256` per archive, one SSHSIG `.sig` per archive, `manifest.json`, and the `install.sh` installer alongside its SSHSIG `install.sh.sig` signature (published and signed with the same release key as the archives). No container image or package-manager formula is published by this pipeline — the gate image is built on the operator's host by `portitor deploy` (see arch_deploy.md).

requirements.title: In-place self-update via the embedded installer
requirements.description: `portitor upgrade` updates the installed `portitor`/`portitor-gate` pair in place, as one unit, by reusing the signed install.sh — embedded into the binary and run in an upgrade mode against the running binary's own path — never a Go reimplementation of the update. install.sh gains an opt-in upgrade mode (--upgrade --target <path>) that keeps its resolve/download/ssh-keygen-Y-verify logic untouched and adds: a safe self-replace (move-aside + rename(2), never install/cp over the running file, to avoid ETXTBSY); a forward-only version guard (equal → already-up-to-date, exit 0; on the latest path — VERSION unset — a resolved latest OLDER than current is a rollback anomaly, hard-refused and NOT overridable, there being no --force; on the explicit path — VERSION set, i.e. --version vX.Y.Z — the named release installs in any direction with an 'as explicitly requested' notice; a signature is authenticity not freshness, so a latest that moved backward is treated as a compromised origin); --rollback (restore <target>.bak, and auto-restore it on any mid-replace failure); --check/--dry-run (report availability only, exit 0 even when latest is older than installed, flagging it as an anomaly WARNING); and RequireRoot with NO auto-sudo (probe target-dir writability and tell the operator to elevate, rather than self-invoking sudo as first-install mode may). first-install mode (no flags) is behaviour-preserving.

requirements.title: The gate binary is installed beside the tool
requirements.description: install.sh, for tool `portitor`, also fetches the release's `linux_<arch>` archive for the host's arch, verifies it against the same release key, and installs its binary as `portitor-gate` beside `portitor` (on a Linux host it is the same archive, fetched once). `--gate-target` names its path (default: beside `--target`). Upgrade and `--rollback` replace and restore both files as one unit, and the pair is up to date only when both are at the target version, so a missing or mismatched `portitor-gate` is repaired; `portitor upgrade` reads `portitor-gate`'s version from its build info and passes it in, because a linux binary cannot be executed on a darwin host. The release artifacts do not change.

requirements.title: Embedded installer is byte-identical to the released one
requirements.description: The canonical install.sh lives at the repo root (uploaded by release.yml, documented in the README). //go:embed cannot traverse '..', so a byte-identical copy is kept at cmd/portitor/install.sh, refreshed by `//go:generate cp ../../install.sh install.sh`, and a Go test (TestUpgradeEmbeddedMatchesReleased) fails the build if the two diverge. This identity is the security argument for self-update: because the embedded script is provably the same audited, signed installer a user runs by hand, `upgrade` needs no separate fetch-and-verify-the-script step — there is nothing to substitute. install.sh also reads test-only PORTITOR_API_BASE/PORTITOR_DL_BASE origin overrides (defaulting to production) so a fake-origin harness can drive the real script; these are not trust-sensitive (verification still gates whatever the origin serves) and the trust anchor SIGNING_PUBKEY is never env-overridable.

requirements.title: Deterministic, ldflags-stamped builds
requirements.description: Builds run with `CGO_ENABLED=0`, `-trimpath`, and linker flags `-s -w` plus `-X main.version=… -X main.commit=… -X main.date=…` sourced from the triggering tag, commit, and build time — so `portitor version` on a downloaded binary reports exactly what it shipped as, with no reliance on runtime environment to reconstruct provenance.

requirements.title: Locally provable before automation runs
requirements.description: The identical `.goreleaser.yaml` and `scripts/generate-manifest.sh` that the release workflow drives also run unmodified via `goreleaser release --snapshot --clean` on a developer machine (snapshot mode skips publish/tag requirements) — the full build → archive → sign → checksum → manifest chain is provable without pushing a tag, holding CI secrets, or touching GitHub Actions.

requirements.title: One idempotent deploy command for the gate
requirements.description: `portitor deploy --config <file>` builds the gate image with Nix and replaces the gate container so that exactly one verified gate runs for the deploy config; an unchanged config rebuilds nothing. The deploy config is a strictly decoded, host-local JSON file holding names and paths, never a secret. Runs under an exclusive per-name lock. See arch_deploy.md.

requirements.title: The gate shares no host path
requirements.description: The gate container's only mounts are two named volumes: the mirrors at /srv/git and the SSH host key at /var/lib/portitor/hostkey. The config dir is the image's top layer at /etc/portitor, root-owned with normalized modes, so nothing the gate reads depends on host file ownership — what a userns-remapped daemon requires.

requirements.title: The image is portitor's fixed part plus the operator's declared tools
requirements.description: The image is a Nix dockerTools.buildLayeredImage over a nixpkgs pin compiled into portitor (overridable per deploy), built for the host's arch on Linux. portitor fixes the runtime, identity, sshd configuration, directories, entrypoint and gate binary; the operator declares only extra tools for their policy commands as {packages, overlay, pin}. portitor bakes no tool any policy names. The tag is a content hash over the rendered expression and every staged input.

requirements.title: The PAT reaches the gate only as a copied-in file
requirements.description: The PAT comes from the deploy config's token_command (stdout) and reaches the gate only as /run/secrets/gh_token, streamed into the created container with docker cp and compared byte for byte after a copy back — never an env var, an argv, an image layer or a host file. GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN are removed from every docker and nix child's environment.

requirements.title: A deploy never leaves the gate worse than it found it
requirements.description: Everything that can refuse — config, gate binary pair and arch, networks, a foreign same-named container, repo config validation as git inside the image, the host-key pin, the PAT — is checked before any container changes. The new gate is created and given its PAT under a temporary name; the previous gate is stopped (not removed) only then, and is restored and restarted if the new one fails to become ready or verified. Volumes are never removed. A later deploy resolves an interrupted one's leftovers by label.

requirements.title: Deploy success is read back, never taken from exit codes
requirements.description: After the swap, deploy reads the state back: the container is running with exactly the two volumes and no GH_TOKEN env; the token file is git-owned 0400; the host key the running sshd serves equals the volume's key and the pin; and, for every repo config with an upstream_slug, GitHub accepts the PAT for that repo. A deploy whose repos have no upstream makes no GitHub call.

requirements.title: The host key persists and is pinned
requirements.description: The gate's ed25519 host key lives in its own volume and survives every recreate. deploy writes it to the pin file on first deploy and refuses when the volume's key differs from the pin, or when the volume is empty while a pin exists. Rotation is explicit: remove the volume and the pin file.

components.name: CIPipeline
components.description: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` + `fuzz.yml` + `acceptance.yml`: the docker tier (userns-remap daemon, Nix installed) on pull_request and push to main; the acceptance tier in `acceptance.yml` on the same triggers, in one global non-cancelling concurrency group; the pull_request/push-to-main fast-then-race gate (go build, go vet, go test, and -race on push only), and the nightly fuzz job that discovers every `func Fuzz*` in the tree at run time via a two-line grep/awk loop (no hardcoded target list) and runs each with a bounded -fuzztime, uploading any failing corpus entry as a workflow artifact on failure.

components.name: ReleasePipeline
components.description: `.goreleaser.yaml` + `.github/workflows/release.yml`: on push of a `v*` tag, cross-compiles linux/darwin × amd64/arm64 via GoReleaser, archives each binary with README.md/LICENSE, computes per-artifact + consolidated sha256 checksums, and publishes the GitHub release — then layers on the per-artifact `.sha256` files, `manifest.json`, and the SLSA provenance attestation that GoReleaser itself does not produce.

components.name: Manifest
components.description: `scripts/generate-manifest.sh`: turns GoReleaser's `dist/artifacts.json` + `dist/metadata.json` into `manifest.json`, self-verifying each artifact's sha256/size from the archive bytes on disk. Generic — the shape is repo-agnostic and portitor defines no bespoke delivery-metadata schema beyond it; `.goreleaser.yaml` is the source of truth this script reads from, never the other way around.

components.name: Signing
components.description: GoReleaser's `signs` block invokes `ssh-keygen -Y sign -n file` (SSHSIG) against each archive with a key the release workflow materializes from the `SSH_SIGNING_KEY` secret into a runner-local temp file (chmod 600; never argv, never a template-expanded command line) and removes afterward, producing one `.sig` per archive. The public key is published in README.md and a verifier checks it with `ssh-keygen -Y verify` against an `allowed_signers` line — the same key and namespace (`-n file`) install.sh embeds, so first-install, maximal, and self-update all trust one anchor. Signing, the consolidated/per-artifact sha256 checksums, and the SLSA attestation are three independent ways to trust a downloaded binary — none is a substitute for another.

components.name: SelfUpdate
components.description: install.sh's upgrade mode (opt-in via --upgrade --target <path> [--gate-target <path>]), replacing the `portitor`/`portitor-gate` pair as one unit, embedded into the binary and driven by `portitor upgrade`: shared resolve/download/SSHSIG-verify with first-install, plus safe self-replace (move-aside + rename to avoid ETXTBSY), a forward-only version guard (equal → no-op; a resolved latest older than installed is a non-overridable rollback-anomaly refusal on the latest path, while an explicitly named --version installs any direction; there is no --force), --rollback, --check (report-only, warns-not-refuses on an older latest), and RequireRoot-no-sudo. Includes the embedded==released byte-identity invariant (cmd/portitor/install.sh via go:generate, enforced by a go test) and the test-only origin hooks. The Go front-end is the cli module's UpgradeCommand.

components.name: Deploy
components.description: `portitor deploy`: the deploy config, the Nix image (fixed part, declared tools, content-hashed tag), and the lock → preflight → build → validate → host key → PAT → create → deliver → swap → wait → verify → commit sequence with rollback. Drives docker and nix as subprocesses. The Go front-end is the cli module's DeployCommand; the entrypoint it embeds is the gate module's Container.
